facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: vṛddho 'ham tvaṁ yuvā dhanvī saraṭhaḥ kavacī śarī | na cāpy ādāya vaidehīṁ kuśalī me gamiṣyasi
facts.text: In the Valmiki Ramayana, Jatayu confronts Ravana by declaring that he is sixty thousand years old, contrasting his aged condition with Ravana's youth, chariot, and armor.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: sa tasya saśaraṁ cāpaṁ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitam | caraṇābhyāṁ mahātejā babhañjasya mahaddhanuḥ
facts.text: Valmiki describes Jatayu swooping upon Ravana and snapping his pearl-and-gem-adorned battle bow in two using both of his clawed feet.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: tataḥ sa hemavicitraṁ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitam | rathaṁ cūrṇayāmāsa pakṣābhyāṁ sa patattrirāṭ
facts.text: The Aranya Kanda states that the vulture king crushed Ravana's gold-inlaid aerial chariot into pieces using his wings and beak.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: kharāṁśca tasya jighāna tūrṇam analasamān... sa sārather asya śiro jahāra
facts.text: Jatayu killed the swift draught beasts pulling the chariot and decapitated Ravana's charioteer with a ferocious blow from his beak.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: sa pakṣau tundacaraṇau savyadakṣiṇakau tadā | chittvā nipātayāmāsa gṛdhrarājam ariṁdamaḥ
facts.text: Valmiki recounts that Ravana dropped to the earth with Sita and drew his sword to sever both wings and flanks of the exhausted vulture.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavation conducted during mid-2018 led to the discovery of several royal burials with chariots, swords and helmets, belong to the Ochre-Coloured Pottery/Copper Hoard culture
facts.text: Excavations conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India at Sinauli uncovered three copper-sheathed wooden wheeled chariots dating to approximately 2000–1800 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Built in the 16th century, the architectural features of the temple are in the Vijayanagara style... It is one of the centrally protected monuments of national importance.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India centrally protects the sixteenth-century Virabhadra Temple complex at Lepakshi, constructed in 1533 CE during the Vijayanagara Empire and tied by local belief to Jatayu.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Lal commenced on another project in 1975 titled, 'Archaeology of the Ramayana sites'. The project was funded by the ASI, Jiwaji University, Gwalior and the Department of Archaeology in the government of Uttar Pradesh.
facts.text: Between 1975 and 1986, the Archaeological Survey of India supported the 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites' project directed by B. B. Lal to excavate material sequences at major settlements associated with the epic.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The archaeologist H. D. Sankalia... read the Vanaras as forest peoples of the peninsula, remembered through the totem or emblem by which they knew themselves.
facts.text: Archaeologist H. D. Sankalia proposed that Jatayu and the Gridhras were an indigenous forest tribe with a vulture totem rather than literal raptors, a theory disputed by traditional commentators who read the epic literally.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: According to local legend, when the wounded Jatayu fell here after his battle against Ravana, Rama said to him, 'Le Pakshi' meaning 'Rise, bird' in Telugu.
facts.text: Regional Andhra folklore holds that the name of Lepakshi originated from Rama comforting the dying raptor with the Telugu words 'Le Pakshi', meaning 'Rise, bird'.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: According to local lore of Kerala, it is believed that Jatayu fell on the rocks in Chadayamangalam in the Kollam district of Kerala after his wings were clipped off by Ravana... features a 61 metres wide statue of Jatayu.
facts.text: A popular local tradition in Kerala identifies the monolithic rock at Chadayamangalam in Kollam as the spot where Jatayu collapsed after Ravana cut off his wings.
